body:
Hello,

Recently, support for [incremental selection](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/34011) has been added to neovim. They choose to use `an` / `in` ("around node" / "inner node") as the default keymaps for this feature. However, this choice conflicts with mini.ai's `around_next` / `inside_next` feature.

I actually wasn't aware mini.ai had this feature (though it is super useful, thanks!), I only found out when I tried using the new LSP selection, and it wasn't working as expected.

Perhaps the defaults should be changed? (I wonder if it also makes sense to change the default `around_last` / `inside_last`)

comment_data.body:
Thanks for notifying. I've only became aware of this change a couple of days ago.

> Perhaps the defaults should be changed?

Yes, on Neovim's side :rofl:

The naming choice is indeed unfortunate for compatibility with 'mini.ai'. I don't think changing defaults in 'mini.ai' is a good idea, because the current keys are the perfect choice.

I think I'd prefer to go the 'miin.operators' route and [automatically remap new built-in `an` / `in`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/48f48e4b3f317e9da34ee7a01958b4c5018e2d34/doc/mini-operators.txt#L114) to something like `aN` / `iN`. Alternatively, users themselves can [adjust these variants in 'mini.ai'](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/48f48e4b3f317e9da34ee7a01958b4c5018e2d34/doc/mini-ai.txt#L437-L441). I'll take a look.

reply_data.body: Probably, not. The approach is the same as in 'mini.operators': do it by default if `an` / `in` will be overridden. If users want to use different keys, they can map directly to them before/after setting up 'mini.ai'. It is a mapping to `vim.lsp.buf.selection_range()` with a proper argument involving `vim.v.count1`. It is shown in `:xmap an` and `:xmap in`.

comment_data.body:
The conflict is now [documented](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/66d3cf727d7bf2ba59df02e710f39640d9af823f/doc/mini-ai.txt#L563-L574) along with the suggested solutions.

I decided to not automatically remap as in 'mini.operators' for several reasons:
- There is no good keys to map to. The `aN` / `iN` will conflict with `N` 'mini.ai' textobjects (which, for example, is recommended for ["number" textobject from 'mini.extra'](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/66d3cf727d7bf2ba59df02e710f39640d9af823f/doc/mini-extra.txt#L90)). The `grs` / `grS` align with built-in LSP mappings, but conflict with 'mini.operators' "replace" operator default `gr` keys.
- It is fairly straightforward to manually map LSP incremental selection. So decided to just document how to map it.

Thanks again for bringing attention to this!
